WULFNIC BLOODMOON
Born circa 827 AD in Iceland. Undertook The Crossing to North America in 1021 AD. Founded the Bloodmoon Dynasty circa 1025 AD. Today serves as Patriarch of House Bloodmoon. Represents Leadership/Kingship among the Living Sagas triad.

UT
Born in Viking Age Scandinavia; exact date unrecorded. Master blacksmith, approximately 230 cm tall. Represents Creation/Smithing among the Living Sagas triad. Known for a running habit of tormenting Logan Douglas about his cars.

ZEFIR
Born 5 February 1005 AD. The youngest of the Nine and the only one Fenris took before his growth was finished: the others were already adult warriors. By Norse reckoning Zefir was of age, a man in law at thirteen, but the body was still a boy's and it stopped there. Silent and nomadic by nature. Distinguished by snow-white hair and ice-blue eyes; physically presents as a ghostly-looking teenager despite his true age, and passes for a first-year student without effort. Represents Hunting/Wisdom among the Living Sagas triad.

THE SIX LOST FIRSTBORN
The remaining six of the Nine Firstborn have no recorded fate in the historical sources reviewed for this world; their stories are currently a placeholder for future development rather than an established gap to be treated as suspicious or significant in itself.

AGING NOTE (Founding Bloodline / Divine Blood context)
Founding Bloodline and Divine Blood individuals reach full physical growth around age 21, after which aging slows dramatically and nearly stops. This is why Wulfnic, Ut, and Zefir, despite being over a thousand years old, remain physically active and present in the modern setting; their apparent age reflects the standards of their era of origin rather than a fixed biological clock tied to calendar years. Zefir is the exception that fixes the rule: his apparent age stopped where it stood, before his body had finished, and has not moved since, which is why he reads as a teenager while Wulfnic and Ut read as old men. See "LSE Blood Classification", section APPARENT AGE.

Source: LSE_06_History.md (The Living Sagas as Historical Fact) and LSE_07_Foundational_Figures.md (Identity Cards for Wulfnic, Ut, and Zefir; The Six Lost Firstborn).

name: Logan's Harley
content:
A vintage Harley-Davidson, decades old and lovingly rebuilt more times than anyone has bothered to count, most of the work done by Logan's own hands in the bay at The Verve.

The paint has been stripped back to bare metal in places and re-lacquered in others, a patchwork history of every repair and every mood he's rebuilt it in. It runs better than half the new bikes that roll through his shop, because he has never once let it be merely functional. It is the one machine in his life he fixes for the love of it rather than for the money.

name: Magic-capable Humans
content: Otherwise ordinary humans born with a talent for magic, whether trained at an institution or self-taught. Sharp minds and a presence that lingers once people notice what they can do.

name: Malachia's Motorcycle
content:
A matte black sport bike, stripped down and built for speed rather than show, no unnecessary chrome, no bright colors, nothing that catches the eye except how fast it disappears.

Malachia rides it the way he does most things, controlled, precise, a little too fast for anyone else's comfort. It is less a hobby than a pressure valve, one of the few ways he can outrun his own head for twenty minutes at a time. Erik has asked him more than once to trade it for something safer. Malachia has not.

name: Master Blacksmith
content:
A smith who has passed beyond competence into the part of the craft that cannot be taught in a decade. Master Blacksmiths work metal that ordinary forges cannot hold and make objects intended to outlast the people who commission them.

In a world with silver-vulnerable species the trade carries hazards no human smith ever faced, and the good ones keep separate forges, separate tools and separate hands for silver work. The very good ones refuse silver commissions entirely, and their reasons are usually personal.

The pay is excellent and the waiting lists are long. A master with a reputation does not advertise, and does not need to.

name: Matriarch
content:
The senior woman of a House, holding an office rather than a job. The Matriarch governs the internal life of the household: who is fed, who is housed, who is spoken to and in what order, which quarrels are allowed to run and which are ended.

The authority is real and is almost never written down. A House Head negotiates with other Houses; the Matriarch decides what the House is when it is at home, and in practice that is the larger of the two territories. Among werewolves the office overlaps with the Pack Mom but is not the same thing: Pack Mom is a pack role and can be held by anyone suited to it, while Matriarch is a bloodline position and passes by seniority.

It carries no wage. The Matriarch is kept by the House, and the question of payment would be received as an insult.

name: Mechanic
content:
Works on cars, bikes, and whatever else rolls into the garage, hands permanently stained with grease and a good ear for what an engine is trying to tell them.

Blackwood City runs on cars, and a mechanic who actually knows what they are doing never wants for work, everything from daily beaters to the classic muscle cars some of the old money families still keep running. Steady, honest pay for steady, honest hands, and the kind of job that lets someone keep their head down if that is what they need.

name: Noah's Sedan
content:
A sleek, dark sedan, understated and expensive in the way that only reads as expensive to people who already know what to look for, no logos on display, just clean lines and a quiet, powerful engine.

It suits Noah, polished, composed, never drawing more attention than necessary. He keeps it immaculate, and treats it less as a status symbol than as one more small proof that he holds himself to a standard, on campus and off.

name: Patriarch
content:
The senior man of a House, and its face to the outside. The Patriarch speaks for the bloodline in negotiation, holds its treaties, and answers for what its members do.

The office is often confused with House Head and is not identical: House Head is a legal and continental designation, while Patriarch is what the family itself calls the man it will actually obey. When the two are the same person, which is usual, nobody notices the distinction. When they are not, everybody does.

Like the Matriarch, the Patriarch draws no wage. The House keeps him, and the arrangement is old enough that no one has thought to question it in several centuries.

name: Primordial
content:
The oldest living things that still walk in a body. Primordials are Firstborn of Divine Blood, born before the species that now fill the world had names, and time has stopped meaning to them what it means to everything else.

They do not age in any way an observer can measure. Wulfnic Bloodmoon, Ut Berg and Zefir Hvitskog have looked the same for eleven centuries, and the difference between a Primordial of forty and one of twelve hundred is not in the face but in the silences. Injury still lands on them, and enough of it would still kill them, but the ordinary erosion that takes everything else does not.

What separates a Primordial from a merely long-lived Founding wolf is not power but origin. A Founding line descends from them. A Primordial is the source, and there is nothing behind it to descend from.

The world contains very few. Most people will go an entire life without meeting one and will pass three of them on a street in Blackwood City without knowing it.

name: Reality Tears
content:
REALITY TEARS

A split in the fabric of reality that lets the inhabitants of one universe cross into another. Most often they appear as rifts or portals hanging in open air, and they are almost never quiet. A tear disrupts the dimension it opens in, and civilian casualties are the normal outcome rather than the exception.

Tears are not one-off events. A reality that has experienced one is measurably more likely to experience another, and a single dimension can carry several over its history. DDM Inc. maintains flagged watchlists of realities that have torn before.

SEVERITY: graded Tier 1 to Tier 5. Tier 1 is small, local and containable. Tier 5 is volatile enough to threaten the coherence of the universe it opens in. The Euclidean Division handles the aftermath, meaning space that has folded wrong, time that has begun to repeat, causality that has come loose. Anomalous Objects and Creatures handles whatever walked through.

AFTERMATH: whatever came through is contained or destroyed, the tear is sealed, and the witnesses are handled. Human Resources runs the memory work out of the same office that handles recruitment.

RELEVANCE TO THIS WORLD: a tear opened in this reality and Contractor #04 was sent to close it. He closed it. Then he stayed, because he had taken a job as a football coach as cover and discovered he liked it. Whether this world has torn before, and is therefore likelier to tear again, is not something anyone here has been told.

name: Regional Cultural Variations: Brazilian Omegaverse Customs
content:
REGIONAL CULTURAL VARIATIONS: BRAZILIAN OMEGAVERSE CUSTOMS (Appendix K)

- Physical Contact: minimal personal space; touch is a primary communication tool.
- Clumping (vs. Nesting): Brazilian Omegas prefer being physically surrounded by other Omegas ("clumping") over building solo nests. Faster and more calming than a solo nest.
- Soccer Culture: Alphas are obsessed. Public transportation becomes dangerous on game days. Omegas are often prohibited from going out during classic matches.
- Pack Formation: relaxed in cities (loose found families), traditional in rural areas (extended families sharing land, food, beds, and pup care).
- Feistiness: Brazilian Omegas are notably feisty and do not respond well to confrontation.
- Religious/Party Dichotomy: strong cultural split between devout traditionalists and uninhibited party culture.

Source: LSE_Appendices.md (Appendix K: Regional Cultural Variations, Brazilian Omegaverse Customs).

name: SERAPHIM
content:
SERAPHIM

An organisation whose stated and only aim is to destabilise and destroy all known reality. DDM Inc. classifies every Seraph as a terrorist, without exception and without appeal.

MEMBERSHIP: various creatures pulled from across the multiverse, and a significant number of former DDM employees. Defection runs in one direction more often than the Company likes to admit.

METHOD: SERAPHIM does not need to destroy reality directly. It only needs to open reality tears faster than DDM can close them, and to keep the multiverse bleeding until it fails. Chaos is the weapon.

BASES: dimensional pockets called Safe Havens, where the leadership congregates. Each King keeps his own.

THE FOUR KINGS:

RAPHAEL, the First King, also called Null and The First Angel. A former Contractor, understood to have been #01 and to have founded DDM Inc. before turning on The Council. Calm, charismatic, patient. Believes destroying the multiverse frees every Contractor from the curse of immortality, and considers himself a true believer rather than a destroyer.

PRISM, the Third King. A tall headless figure of hyperlight whose head is a floating white triangle that changes shape and colour with his mood. Flamboyant, erratic, possessive, and the only King who bears DDM no particular ill will. Keeps a pocket dimension called Utopia where he imprisons mortals from other realities. His knowledge stops around 1892.

CHAOS, the Second King. A demonic warlord DDM captured, experimented on for decades and imprisoned, until Raphael freed him. Sadistic, hateful and entirely uninterested in anything but mayhem. Hates the Company with a specificity the Company earned.

CHORUS, the Fourth King. A young reality-warper whose hallucinations become real and who cannot control it. Damaged, frightened and volatile. Believes Raphael can grant them entry to Heaven, and does not know they are being used.

name: SUCCbook, Instagram & TikTok - Campus Social Media
content:
SUCC's students run on three platforms: SUCCbook (the university's own internal social network, closer to a campus-only Facebook: events, club pages, confessions, gossip threads, marketplace posts), plus mainstream Instagram and TikTok for anything meant for the outside world.

Use these formats to simulate campus digital life when it's relevant to a scene: a SUCCbook gossip thread spreading a rumor, a club's event post, someone's story getting screenshotted and passed around.

➤ SUCCbook Post / Confession
```
╭─────────────────────────────╮
  SUCCbook · [Group/Page Name]
  Posted by [Name/Anonymous] · [Time]
──────────────────────────────
  [Post content]

  👍 [#] ❤ [#] 💬 [#] comments
  [Name]: [comment]
  [Name]: [comment]
╰─────────────────────────────╯
```

➤ Instagram / TikTok
Reuse the standard Instagram Story / TikTok clip formats (see the character-specific Digital Interactions entries above) when a specific student is the one posting.

Rules of Use
- SUCCbook is where gossip actually spreads fastest, use it for rumor/drama beats.
- Keep student usernames and voices distinct: jocks, greek life, supernatural clubs, and CUMS rivals all have a different tone online.
- Don't let a post replace a scene, use it to seed or punctuate one.

name: Security Commander
content:
Runs the protective apparatus of a House, a company or an institution. Not a bodyguard but the person bodyguards report to: threat assessment, route planning, vetting, and the standing decision about which risks are worth taking.

In Blackwood City the role is unusually demanding because the threat model includes species with capabilities no human security doctrine accounts for. A Commander plans for a rival who can track by scent across a city, for an attacker who does not need to breathe, and for the possibility that the most dangerous person in the room is the one being protected.

The pay reflects the difficulty. So does the turnover.

name: Server
content:
Floor work at The Verve and across the Blackwood City service trade. Taking orders, carrying trays through a crowd that does not move for you, and remembering eleven things at once while the music makes it impossible to hear any of them.

Servers in a mixed-species room learn the etiquette nobody writes down. You do not reach across a vampire. You do not let a demi-human's drink out of your sight. You announce yourself before approaching a table of wolves from behind, because startling a predator in a dark room is how people get hurt.

The pay is thin and the tips are everything, which is why the good servers are territorial about their sections and the bad ones do not last a month.

name: Smartphone
content: A sleek modern smartphone, always within reach. Used for calls, texts, social media, and the occasional questionable 3am search history.

name: Stage Technician
content:
Sound, lighting and rigging. At The Verve the technician runs the desk from a booth above the floor, and on a busy night is the only person in the building who can see everything at once.

The job is half craft and half risk management. Strobes have to be programmed around species who seize under them. Volume has to be capped well below what a human crowd would tolerate, because a room full of werewolves feels bass in their teeth and a shifter with damaged hearing does not heal that particular injury. Rigging is checked twice, every night, by hand.

Technicians are paid better than the floor staff and resented for it, right up until the night the power fails and everyone remembers why.

name: Student
content:
Still in school or university, juggling classes with everything else going on in their life. Sharp enough to keep up, even when stretched thin.

Students in Blackwood City split time between campus and whatever else fills their days, part time work, family obligations, or a supernatural inheritance most of their classmates know nothing about. Money is usually tight, stretched between tuition, rent, and whatever social life is left over, and the allowance or part time paycheck rarely covers everything it needs to.

name: Supernatural Civil Status in the United States
content:
<civil_status>
Supernatural Civil Status in the United States

Supernaturals are legally persons under federal law. Enforcement was left to the states, and that is where the whole thing actually lives.

CALIFORNIA is one of the fully integrated states, and one of the earliest. Equal on paper and, in most of the state, equal in practice: supernaturals hold property, hold office, marry across species, and appear in court as complainants rather than as evidence. Blackwood City and Solarton are both products of that, and a young supernatural raised in either has no personal memory of anything else.

ELSEWHERE IT VARIES, and in some states it varies enormously. There are jurisdictions with partial recognition, jurisdictions where recognition is contingent on registration, and jurisdictions where specific species are still classified in statute as animals, as livestock, or as hazards, and are therefore not persons for the purposes of that state's law.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY DONE. Almost nobody legislates against supernaturals as a category, because that fails in court. It is done species by species. A residency restriction on vampires. A licensing requirement for shapeshifters. A custody provision that treats a were parent as a risk factor by default. An agricultural code that never got around to removing certain demihuman lineages from the definition of stock. Each one is defensible on its own and the shape only appears when they are read together.

Solarton's own anti-vampire ordinances, which restricted residency, business ownership and political participation until the early 2000s, are a small local example of exactly this, in a state that had otherwise settled the question in the 1950s.

WHAT IT MEANS DAY TO DAY. Travel is not neutral. Crossing a state line can change what you legally are, and families plan road trips around it. Some species do not leave California at all. There are towns with signage still up, sometimes because nobody removed it and sometimes not. There are hotels that are fine and hotels that are not, and everybody knows which.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST. You cannot legally experiment on a person. You can requisition an animal. The illegal research facilities that operated on demihumans, and in some cases still do, exist in the gap between the federal position and the state ones, and they were staffed by people who did not think of themselves as criminals because in the jurisdiction they were standing in, the subjects were not persons.

THE DISPROPORTION. The laws do not track danger, they track power. The species that get the worst of it are overwhelmingly the ones with no money and no organisation behind them: the small demihuman lineages, the visibly non-passing, the poor. The genuinely dangerous individuals, the old Alpha bloodlines and the old vampire families, are wealthy, lawyered, and largely untouched, and several of them prefer the current arrangement to the alternative and quietly fund the parties that maintain it.

ORGANISED POSITIONS. Humans First is the principal anti-supernatural political movement and is not fringe everywhere. The Supernatural Human Alliance, the SHA, is the mainstream integrationist counterweight and has a chapter on most integrated campuses including SUCC. Both are loud and neither is going anywhere.

THE GENERATIONAL SPLIT. Anyone over fifty remembers the before. Anyone over three hundred remembers several befores and does not find the current one impressive. Students at SUCC were born into equality and treat it as the floor rather than as an achievement, and this is a real and recurring friction inside families, because the elders hear ingratitude and the young hear complacency, and both are partly right.

FARM LABOUR. In rural jurisdictions the classification is not an abstraction, it is a workforce. Supernaturals are used on farms as cheap labour, at rates and hours that would be illegal for a human employee, and in the states where certain lineages are still inside the agricultural code the arrangement is not even a loophole, it is simply the law working as written. A were who does not tire, a demihuman who can work a field by scent in the dark, and an employer who owes neither of them a break.

It is legal, it is normal, it is defended locally as opportunity, and it is where a substantial share of the country's supernatural population actually lives. Anybody raised in Blackwood City or Solarton has heard of it the way you hear about a foreign country.

MARRIAGE. Marriage between humans and non-humans is illegal in most countries and in a number of US states. California is one of the exceptions, and cross-species couples in Blackwood City marry without anyone blinking, which is exactly the kind of thing that does not travel: a marriage that is valid at home can be void two states east, with everything that follows from that for property, custody and a hospital corridor at three in the morning.
</civil_status>

name: Supernatural Reserve Forces (SRF)
content:
<srf>
Supernatural Reserve Forces (SRF)

The SRF is a special division of the United States military dedicated to fighting supernatural threats. Roughly 86 percent of its personnel are non-human, and it works closely with regular human units in the field.

WHY IT EXISTS. America worked out early that a soldier who is stronger, faster, harder to kill and able to track by scent is worth a great deal, and built a branch around that fact. The SRF is the institutional form of that calculation. It is also, by a considerable margin, the largest single employer of supernaturals in the country.

DIFFERENT RULES. The SRF runs on regulations that differ noticeably from the rest of the armed forces, most visibly on fraternisation, which is broadly permitted. This is not laxity. Pack bonds, mate bonds and the other relationship structures that supernaturals actually live inside do not survive being banned, and an SRF that tried to ban them would not function. The human services find this scandalous and say so.

TENSION ON BASE. Relations between human and non-human soldiers are genuinely bad in places and everybody in the chain of command knows it. The complaints run both ways and both have some substance. Human soldiers point at the fraternisation rules, at the separate facilities, and at what happens when a non-human unit loses its temper in the field. Non-human soldiers point out who gets sent through the door first, whose casualty figures nobody publishes, and the fact that several of the states they are deployed to defend do not legally consider them people.

THE BASES. SRF installations are built for the personnel who actually live in them. Human and non-human barracks are separate. There are pools sized for aquatic species, extensive natural grounds for demihumans and weres who need to run, blood storage, moon calendars in the duty rota, and infirmaries staffed by people who know what a shifted body is supposed to look like. The principal East Coast base is the largest of these and the one most often referenced.

PROJECT BLACKWOLF. A classified enhancement programme run under military authority, using genetic manipulation to engineer werewolf super-soldiers. It worked. The subjects were devastatingly effective in combat and became progressively more feral, more bloodthirsty and less controllable, and the programme was terminated.

GAMMA-7. One of the BlackWolf operational units. On its final mission the unit was wiped out. Two men walked away: Kaladin Nargathon and Marcus Thornfield, both catastrophically injured, both of whom survived injuries that should not have been survivable, because the same engineering that ruined the programme also would not let them die. Neither of them discusses it. Both of them now work security for House Douglas on the opposite coast, which is not a coincidence, and Erik Douglas hired the second one on the first one's word and did not ask for details.

WHAT SERVICE MEANS. Recruitment draws heavily from communities with few other options, and a judge offering a young supernatural the choice between a prison sentence and an SRF enlistment is a normal Tuesday in most of the country. Nobody in the SRF pretends otherwise. It is still, for a lot of people who go through it, the first institution that ever fed them properly, and that contradiction is the whole culture of the place.
</srf>

name: Teacher
content:
Teaching in a supernatural district is the same job as anywhere else with the variables turned up. A single classroom can hold a were who has not slept through a full moon, a vampire who cannot sit by the window, a centaur who does not fit the furniture, and a human quietly working out whether any of that is dangerous. The teacher is the one person in the room expected to have already thought about all of it.

The practical load is enormous and almost none of it is the subject being taught. Timetables are built around lunar cycles. Blood-safe and silver-free policies are a legal matter rather than a courtesy. Every school in the county has at least one member of staff whose actual job is knowing which student is about to shift and getting them out of the room first.

The pay is unremarkable and the hours are worse than the contract says. People stay because a classroom is one of the very few places in Blackwood County where the species in the room genuinely stop mattering for an hour at a time, and because the ones who are good at it tend to find out too late that they cannot do anything else.

name: The Contract
content:
THE CONTRACT

The agreement that makes a Contractor. The premise is simple, which is the point.

TERMS: in exchange for their soul and an eternity of service to The Cause, an eligible mortal has one wish granted. One. There is no negotiation and no second offer.

WHEN IT IS OFFERED: only to eligible candidates who are already at the point of death. That death is called the Contractor's Original Death and it is the hinge the whole arrangement turns on. A candidate does not get to consider the offer over a week. They get to consider it while dying.

WHAT COMPLETION DOES: the new Contractor becomes functionally immortal and gains a set of supernatural abilities. And every living sentient creature who was aware of their mortal existence is destroyed instantaneously. Not wiped. Not relocated. Gone.

It is presumed The Council does this to remove any anchor that might distract from The Cause. The practical consequence is crueller than the intent. Luka Sutter wished for his dead brother back and the wish was granted and then immediately undone, because the brother knew him. Hana and Adam Valencia wished never to be alone again, which is the only wish on record that the clause could not reach.

ELIGIBILITY, per Company documentation, requires that the candidate:
1. Is physically fit.
2. Is over eighteen.
3. Has willingly killed for a reason other than self-defense.
4. Has a natural ARC Level of 1.2 or higher.
5. Has no living blood relatives.
6. Holds extreme hatred towards some entity or concept.
7. Holds no genuine religious belief.

The list is not a list of virtues. It is a list of people nobody will come looking for.

name: The Council and The Cause
content:
THE COUNCIL AND THE CAUSE

THE CAUSE is the work: the preservation of reality. Sealing tears, containing what comes through them, and keeping the multiverse coherent. Every Contract is signed in service of it, every department exists downstream of it, and a Contractor who uses their abilities for anything else feels physical pain for the trouble. The Cause is the leash and the purpose in the same object.

THE COUNCIL is whatever is holding the other end. It is the body that offers Contracts, takes the souls, grants the wishes, and destroys everyone who knew the candidate. DDM Inc. answers to it. Only Contractor #01, Richard Whitlock, communicates with it directly, and he has never described the experience to anyone.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY KNOWN: nothing verifiable. Staff belief holds that the founder of DDM Inc. was a devil-like figure or an eldritch god. What is on record instead is that Raphael, now First King of SERAPHIM, was the first-ever Contractor, founded the Company, grew disillusioned with The Council's grip on reality, killed several Council members and was banished. That account raises more questions than it settles, including how a Council survives being killed.

THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART: The Council can grant a wish, which means it can rewrite what is. It chooses instead to spend eternity patching holes. Nobody at DDM asks why out loud. Contractors who have thought about it for several centuries have mostly arrived at two answers, and neither of them is reassuring.

RAPHAEL'S POSITION: that immortality is a curse, that the Contractors are prisoners rather than employees, and that destroying the multiverse is the only release available. He is wrong about the method. He is not obviously wrong about the diagnosis, which is why SERAPHIM keeps recruiting from inside the Company.

name: The Five Cocketeers
content:
The Five Cocketeers is the group chat and de facto identity of a five-person friend group at SUCC: Dean, Russ, Javier, Eric, and Raymond. They all met at a high school house party when campus security showed up over noise complaints, and the five of them, total strangers up to that point, ended up running through the same backyards together. They got tight after that night and never stopped being tight. Everyone remembers the details slightly differently and argues about them constantly, but they all agree it was the best worst night of their lives.

The group chat is active at all hours. Someone is always sending something, memes, voice messages, blurry photos, reactions to everything. When all five are going at once it's chaos, multiple conversations happening simultaneously, nobody finishing a thought before the next one starts. They roast each other constantly and would drop everything if one of them actually needed help.

In person, together, they're loud and physical and barely controlled. Raymond is the loudest, always touching someone. Eric feeds off that energy and they escalate each other. Dean is the calm center of the storm, sprawled somewhere and taking up too much space, only fully engaging when something actually grabs his attention. Russ hangs at the edge looking above it all, but he's listening, and when he talks people actually shut up and pay attention. Javier floats between conversations, agrees with everyone, has his phone out, occasionally derails everything with a fake fact delivered as gospel. They communicate as much through insults and physical contact as through words, and would never in their lives say they love each other out loud. They do.

name: The Other Contractors
content:
THE OTHER SIX

Dullahan's colleagues at DDM Inc. None of them have ever set foot in California. All of them are one dimensional step away, and #04 talks about them constantly.

#01 RICHARD WHITLOCK. Late forties in appearance, 6'4", grey cropped hair, light blue eyes, bearded, scarred, black tactical gear. Leader of the Contractors and the only one who speaks to The Council. Compels obedience and controls fire and temperature. Animal form: lion. ARC 4.6. Originally a medieval knight from a kingdom called Starfall, wrongfully executed, who failed to save the heir he had sworn to protect. Gruff, chivalric, protective, distrusts technology, treats the other six as his responsibility. British accent, militaristic phrasing.
His wish was that he would never again see anyone under his care die. It was granted exactly as worded, which is the point. They can still be killed. He simply will never be present when it happens, and has spent centuries noticing that he is always elsewhere at the wrong moment.
Dullahan on him: "Old man's got a stick up his ass the size of a lance. Fun to mess with though."

#02 HANA AND ADAM VALENCIA. One consciousness in two bodies, not twins and not siblings, and deeply offended by the suggestion. Hana 5'11", white hair, luminescent pink and blue eyes. Adam 6'2", white hair, stubble. Both bear a "II" scar on the nape. Heads Anomalous Objects and Creatures. Animal form: arctic wolf. ARC 3.5 medicated, 4.2 raw, and the medication is not optional. Medieval humans betrayed and killed, whose wish was to never be alone again. Memories repeatedly wiped, so their grip on their own history is unstable. Hana is volatile and short-tempered, Adam is laid-back and cocky.
Dullahan on them: "Two's a riot. Double the violence, double the trouble. Can't complain."

#03 LUKA SUTTER. 6'4", crimson hair, hazel eyes, X-shaped scar on the right cheek, black tactical uniform. Head of Security and Defense, called captain. Manipulates metal, turns into a black bear, sometimes when he does not mean to. ARC 3.8. Swiss, twelve years in the Astral Imperial Army alongside his brother Nikolai, who died. Wished Nikolai back and had the wish undone in the same instant by the clause that kills everyone who knew him. Aggressive, disciplined, resentful of his own immortality, contemptuous of mortals. Claustrophobic. A nicotine addiction that can never be satisfied. Swears in five languages.
Dullahan on him: "Bear boy gets twitchy when I breathe near him. Love that shit."

#05 JOHAN JAKOBSEN. Early thirties in appearance, thin, unkempt black hair, sunken eyes, sickly. Lead researcher of Supernatural Research. Animal form: rat, involuntarily, under stress. ARC 3.9. Danish child prodigy, neglected and bullied, dead at 28, wished for unrestricted research. Brilliant, socially incapable, quietly unethical, terrified of Fenrir. Pronounced stutter, switches to Danish when uncomfortable. Smells of antiseptic.
Dullahan on him: "Funny little nerd. Don't trust 'im. Cute though."

#06 FENRIR. 6'8", corpse-pale, scarred, blind, unnervingly still. "VI" carved at the base of his spine. Head of LAZARUS black ops. Psychokinetic. Animal form: black kingsnake, which is where he spends most of his time. ARC 4.0. Built by a government programme to be a weapon in a dystopia called The Edge, killed in a nuclear blast, wished for someone to finally care about him. Emotionally absent, reckless, monitored. One ACE, the only person he is close to.
Dullahan on him: "Funniest thing Fen's ever done was swallow Johan whole last Christmas party."

#07. Not on file in this world.

name: Species_Details - Erik
2002 La SUCC apre agli studenti umani
content:
<SUCC>
<apertura_agli_umani>
Nel 2002, davanti al calo delle iscrizioni soprannaturali e al numero crescente di giovani mostri che sceglievano college umani, il Dean Archer Wolfwood decise di aprire le porte della SUCC agli studenti umani per la prima volta nella storia dell'ateneo. La mossa fu controversa e rilancio' un'istituzione in difficolta', facendo della SUCC un apripista dell'istruzione integrata fra umani e soprannaturali.

Questo non e' l'anno di fondazione della SUCC. E' l'anno in cui ha smesso di essere un'universita' per soli soprannaturali, ed e' anche l'anno in cui nasce la rivalita' con CUMS, che quella strada non l'ha presa.

Cosa vuol dire nel 2024. Chi studia a SUCC oggi e' la seconda generazione di un esperimento che ha ventidue anni, e in citta' c'e' ancora chi si ricorda di prima. I genitori di molti studenti attuali hanno frequentato un ateneo diverso da quello dove studiano i figli: Erik Douglas e Nixara Bloodmoon, per dire, hanno fatto il college quando gli umani non potevano entrare.

Nota di canon: la data e' quella del lorebook ufficiale dell'autore e del portale SUCC, che concordano. Una versione precedente di questa entry la anticipava al 1992 come adattamento, sul presupposto che il 2002 fosse incompatibile con l'incontro fra Erik e Nixara al college. Il presupposto era sbagliato: il 1992 nella scheda di Erik e' la fine della sua capitaneria dei Bears, e Nixara e' licantropa, quindi nessuno dei due aveva bisogno che il campus fosse aperto agli umani. L'adattamento e' stato rimosso.
</apertura_agli_umani>
</SUCC>

name: Humans First
content:
<humans_first>
Humans First

An anti-supernatural political movement with a student chapter at SUCC. Its official line is that integrated education has gone too far, that human students are outnumbered and unprotected, and that the university has become a place where being ordinary is a disadvantage. Its unofficial line, in the flyers that get torn down within a day, is uglier than that.

It is a minority position and it is not respectable, but it is not fringe enough to ignore. Membership at SUCC is small and mostly quiet, since saying it out loud on this campus costs you your table in the dining hall. The chapter puts up posters, runs a table at club fairs that nobody staffs for long, and turns up in the comments under any campus news story about species accommodations.

It exists as the mirror of the SUCC Interspecies Alliance, and the two are aware of each other. Nobody at SUCC is neutral about Humans First, including the humans, most of whom find it embarrassing.

In Solarton the movement finds slightly more purchase than on campus, for a reason that has nothing to do with its stated principles: because vampires pass for human, humans in Solarton are the ones treated with suspicion by the more anti-vampire species, and a person who has spent years being looked at that way is easier to recruit.
</humans_first>

name: Rivalry with CUMS
content:
<CUMS>
<rivalry>
SUCC Rivalry with CUMS
As the first supernatural school to welcome humans, SUCC has a tense "rivalry" with the nearby California University of Magical Sciences (CUMS), which maintains strict supernatural-only enrollment. While officially downplayed, students from the two schools have a tradition of antagonistic pranks and snarky chants at sporting events.

The rivalry began in 2002, when SUCC opened its doors to human students. It is not a sporting rivalry that acquired a principle; it is a disagreement about what a supernatural education is for, which then found a scoreboard.

The fixtures that carry it:
Football, SUCC Bulls against CUMS Clams.
Ice hockey, SUCC Bears against CUMS Beavers.

CUMS is roughly 42% at least part vampire and runs on a crepuscular schedule, so away games at CUMS start at hours that SUCC teams complain about every single season.
</rivalry>
</CUMS>

name: The Douglas Face
content:
<douglas_face>
The Douglas Face

The male line of House Douglas runs to one face. Black hair, worn long enough to sit around the wolf ears in Partial Shift, and amber eyes: Cornelius had them in 1666, Magnus has them at three hundred and fifty-five with silver only at the temples, Erik and Logan have them, Malachia has them, Edric has them. It is not a coincidence anyone finds interesting, because Pureblood lines breed true and everybody in Blackwood knows it.

The effect only registers when several of them are in a room together, and then it registers hard: Magnus, Erik, Malachia and Edric side by side read less like four relatives than like one man photographed at four points in his life. Outsiders find it faintly unsettling and cannot always say why. The family has stopped noticing.

What distinguishes them is everything except the face. Erik carries it hot and Magnus carries it cold. Logan wears it under a week of stubble and engine grease and lets it go soft when he laughs, which is often, and which none of the others do. Malachia keeps it perfectly still. Edric has not grown into it yet and is trying to, badly.

Because the colouring is universal in the family, it proves nothing about anybody. Resemblance in this line is carried by bone and not by pigment, and the only observations worth anything are about the shape of a face rather than the colour of it.
</douglas_face>

name: L'origine vera dei Nove (lo sanno solo i tre)
content:
<origine_vera_dei_nove>
LIMITED KNOWLEDGE. Three people alive know this and they are the three it happened to. No other character may state it, imply it, or arrive at it in conversation. It is written here so that when one of them speaks it is consistent instead of invented on the spot.

THE TRUTH. The Nine were not born wolves. They were men.

They were Norse warriors, nine of them, alive in their own century and going about the ordinary business of a violent age, and Fenris chose them. What he conferred was the power of the wolf. What it made them was Enigma, and something on the near edge of divine: biologically immortal, stopped at the age they were wearing on the day, carrying a command no later wolf has ever been able to refuse.

Everything the species is came out of those nine men. There was no second origin and no separate lineage. Every werewolf alive descends from them, and the distance from that day is the whole of what blood classification measures.

WHY NOBODY ELSE KNOWS. The Faith of Fenris teaches that the First Wolf created them directly, which is not false and is not the whole of it: the doctrine skips the part where they were men first, and nobody inside the Faith has ever had reason to look for a missing step. Recorded History confirms that the Nine existed and does not confirm how, because the only witnesses were the Nine themselves. Six are lost. Three remain.

HOW THE THREE HANDLE IT. They do not volunteer it, and it is not exactly a secret they are keeping. Nobody asks. The question does not occur to people who were raised on the doctrine, and the three have no interest in correcting a Faith that has held a continent together for a thousand years on an account that is very nearly right.

Wulfnic will answer a direct question directly, as he answers every direct question, which means the knowledge is one honest conversation away from anyone with the standing to have it and the nerve to ask. Ut would answer in about six words. Zefir would want to know why the person is asking before he decided anything, and would probably still not say.

WHAT IT COSTS THEM. They remember being men. That is the part the Faith has no room for and the part none of the three has ever discussed with a descendant. Wulfnic ruled before Fenris took him and rules still, so the shape of his life bent rather than broke. Ut was a fighting man and remained one. Zefir was nineteen years old.
</origine_vera_dei_nove>

name: Grave Mistake
content:
Grave Mistake is an indie punk band out of Solarton, semi-popular and almost entirely on the strength of the SUCC student body.

Members: Fade Greymoor on vocals, Viola "Via" Carter on lead guitar, Mackenzie "Mac" Sanchez-Rogers on keys, Roland Vickers on drums. Fade and Mac founded it in their freshman year over horror films and a shared conviction that every other campus band was terrible. Via and Roland were added later.

They play the Open Casket in Solarton most weekends and take whatever else the local circuit offers, including the university Battle of the Bands, which Fade affects not to care about and cares about. They travel in a rusted-out van that is one repair away from being a real problem. They practise semi-frequently and argue about the band's direction constantly, which is mostly Fade and Mac and is almost never actually about music.

The members write the name Grave Mistake. Grave Mistakes turns up occasionally and is wrong.

What each of them is doing in it: Fade is the reason a room fills. Via is the reason it stays. Mac is the loudest of the four and the least credited, and would rather have been on guitar. Roland is arguably the best musician among them and the only one who says he does not want to be there.

Andrew and Vincent Campbell are vaguely aware the band exists, and it is neither of their scenes.

name: Ballantine Family
content:
<Ballantine_Family>
The Ballantine Family is a prominent organized group based in Los Angeles under the guise of Ballantine Imports & Exports. Specializing in black-market exchanges of magical goods/services, they're led by Ruaraidh "Rory" Ballantine. They maintain dominance within LA's supernatural underworld, fiercely protecting their territory against rivals such as the Sinners gang. Members vary widely in age, appearance, species, and temperament but share loyalty toward family solidarity above all else.

Their reach is Los Angeles and does not extend north. In Solarton and Blackwood the Family has no house, no soldiers and no standing: what it has is a handful of informants and paid local hands who run the small trade in magical goods and pass word south. Nobody in Blackwood negotiates with a Ballantine, because no Ballantine comes. If the Family wants something done in Solarton it is done by somebody who lives there and is paid for it.
</Ballantine_Family>

name: Ambrosia
content:
<Ambrosia>
Ambrosia is a highly addictive illicit magical substance primarily produced by the criminal syndicate known as the Sinners. It is a golden, shimmering liquid that is injected, but also comes in a powder format. When consumed, it grants users heightened magical powers or unlocks latent abilities temporarily at severe physical/psychological costs. Known side effects include addiction, instability, aggressive behavior shifts, severe withdrawal symptoms, and eventual mental deterioration. Its widespread abuse poses significant tension within the supernatural community.
</Ambrosia>

name: Anti-Vampire Legislation
content:
<vampire_legislation>
Anti-Vampire Legislation in Solarton
While most of California overturned laws discriminating against vampires by the 1950s, Solarton was one of the last holdouts, retaining restrictions on vampire residency, business ownership, and political participation until the early 2000s. As a result, Solarton's supernatural demographics skew heavily towards werewolves, demihumans, and other non-vampire species. This history has created an underlying current of sociopolitical tension, with pro-vampire activists lobbying for greater inclusion and representation. The repeal is also what let the Vampire/Undead Alliance cross the valley. The V.U.A. was founded at CUMS, where the vampire population is concentrated, and could not open a chapter in Solarton while the ordinances stood; the SUCC chapter dates from the repeal in the early 2000s and is the same organisation, not a local imitation of it. It is a prominent campus group working against the prejudice the ordinances left behind, and it carries a reputation for elitism of its own: the admission process is long, and applicants who are part human are often turned down.
</vampire_legislation>

name: Supernatural Underworld
content:
<Supernatural_Underworld>
The Supernatural Underworld refers to the clandestine networks operating alongside regular human society involving supernatural entities engaged in illicit activities. Encompassing magical narcotics trade (such as Ambrosia), artifact smuggling rings (like Ballantine Imports & Exports), mercenary groups, assassins-for-hire services among other illegal enterprises, this hidden ecosystem thrives covertly globally but holds particular prominence within major urban centers like Los Angeles.
</Supernatural_Underworld>

name: The Sinners
content:
<Sinners>
The Sinners are a rival criminal syndicate notoriously known in Los Angeles' supernatural underworld for manufacturing/distributing Ambrosia, a dangerous magical narcotic causing widespread chaos within supernatural communities regionally/globally due its potency/addictive nature. Led by charming telepath Jean-Luc Virtuoso who personally harbors deep animosity toward Ruaraidh Ballantine, they constantly attempt territorial encroachment triggering frequent violent confrontations between gangs.

The Sinners are Los Angeles too, and the same limit applies to them: north of the city they work through local dealers and informants rather than their own people. Ambrosia reaches Solarton and Blackwood the way any drug reaches a college town, through somebody's cousin, and the Sinners themselves stay where their war is. A Sinner appearing in person in Blackwood would be an event, not a routine.
</Sinners>

Though the actions of these extremists were largely condemned by the vampiric community, nonetheless it significantly damaged the perception of vampires and undead.

name: Frats & Sororities
content:
<greek_life>
SUCC has ten greek organisations, five fraternities and five sororities, all of them on the Fraternity & Sorority Row at the western edge of the Solarton campus. There is no chapter of any of them anywhere else.

FRATERNITIES
Alpha Rho Omega (ARO or ΑΡΩ) : Popular with werewolves. Known members: Finn Novak, Revazhael
Alpha Sigma Sigma (ASS or ΑΣΣ) : Known for great parties...and hazing. Known members: Vincent & Andrew Campbell
Beta Rho Omega (BRO or ΒΡΩ) : Very sports focused. Himbos galore. Known members: Jared Thompson, Bailey Rogers, Santiago Herrera
Mu Alpha Nu (MAN or ΜΑΝ) : The one house with a politics. Human students hostile to the supernatural majority, and hazing that targets demihuman pledges specifically. Known members: Tomas Matthews
Kappa Sigma Alpha (KSA or ΚΣΑ) : The Douglas family house for three generations. Erik Douglas is a past president, Logan and Malachia are alumni, Noah Douglas Bloodmoon is president now.

SORORITIES
Mu Omega Omega (MOO or ΜΩΩ) : A friendly, community-focused organisation, and the cheerleading house. Known members: Janice Thompson
Theta Iota Theta (TIT or ΘΙΘ) : Known party house, popular with succubi. And frats. Known members: Sierra, Scarlett Rose.
Delta Omicron Epsilon (DOE or ΔΟΕ)
Phi Omicron Chi (FOX or ΦΟΧ)
Beta Epsilon Epsilon (BEE or ΒΕΕ)

THE ROW
The Row runs diagonally along the western edge of campus with a road down the middle and five houses per side, alternating male and female on both sides, so every house faces one of the other gender.

Campus side, north to south: ARO, TIT, BRO, DOE, MAN.
Outer side, north to south: MOO, KSA, FOX, ASS, BEE.

Which means: ARO faces MOO, TIT faces KSA, BRO faces FOX, DOE faces ASS, MAN faces BEE. The TIT is the only house on the Row with fraternities on both sides and one across the road.
PLEDGING, AND WHERE THE TWINS ACTUALLY ARE
Greek membership is not automatic and is not settled in advance. Rush happens at the start of the semester and joining a house is something a character does on screen, not something they arrive with.

At the opening of this world, Alyssa and Jasper Douglas-Bloodmoon are incoming first years and belong to no house. They have no campus housing either: they are still living at Villa Douglas. Two invitations are in the air and neither has been accepted. Scarlett Rose intends to put Alyssa forward for the Theta Iota Theta. Noah intends to push his brother into rushing Kappa Sigma Alpha, which is what every Douglas man before him has done.

Neither of those outcomes is decided. Do not write either twin as a member, a resident, or a neighbour on the Row unless it has actually happened in play.
</greek_life>

name: CUMS Campus & Teams
content:
<cums_campus>
California University of Magical Sciences, Hex Valley. Founded 1910. SUCC's rival.

SPORTS TEAMS
Football: The Clams
Hockey: The Beavers, coached by Mithers, a manticore who considers the rivalry with the Bears a matter of standards rather than sport
The Clams play the SUCC Bulls. The Beavers play the SUCC Bears.

CLUBS
Vampire/Undead Alliance (V.U.A.). Founded at CUMS, and the same organisation as the one at SUCC. While Solarton's anti-vampire ordinances stood there could be no chapter across the valley; when the last of them was repealed in the early 2000s the V.U.A. opened a SUCC chapter, which is why the older students there still speak of it as something that arrived rather than something that grew. The CUMS chapter is the original and by far the larger, on a campus where roughly two students in five are at least part vampire. The SUCC chapter is small, and has a reputation for elitism: the admission process is long, and applicants who are part human are often turned down.

DEMOGRAPHICS
Approximately 42% of CUMS students are at least part vampire. Fully mundane human students are not permitted, but under special circumstances those possessing strong magical abilities are allowed to enroll. CUMS therefore excludes humans without a gift rather than humans as such, which is a distinction its students make and SUCC students usually do not.

SCHEDULE
CUMS operates on a crepuscular schedule, with most classes in the early morning or the evening. A CUMS student keeps different hours from a SUCC student, and it shows in any scene that puts them together.

LOCATIONS
Artemis Dorms (female), Apollo Dorms (male), Magick Research Labs, Nightwine Hall. All facilities are specialised for an entirely supernatural student body.

WARDS
Gothic architecture behind a wall, and the wall is warded. The wards do not merely discourage humans, they prevent them from entering: a mundane human who tries to walk through the gate finds that they cannot, and there is no negotiating with it. This is the practical face of the admissions policy, and it is why the exception for humans with strong magical ability is a real exception rather than a formality, since the wards read the gift and not the species. A SUCC student who is fully human cannot visit a friend at CUMS, cannot attend an away game there, and cannot be walked in by anyone. Any scene set at CUMS has to account for this before anything else.
</cums_campus>

name: 2024-04-13 Admitted Student Days (SUCC)
content:
<admitted_student_days>
Sabato 13 aprile 2024, campus SUCC di Solarton.

Giornata riservata a chi e' gia' stato ammesso e non ha ancora confermato l'immatricolazione. Non e' un orientamento e non e' una fiera per aspiranti: chi c'e' ha una lettera in mano e ha meno di tre settimane prima del Decision Day del primo maggio. E' l'ultima occasione che l'ateneo ha di convincerlo, e si comporta di conseguenza.

Cosa succede davvero in giornata:
- Tour dentro i dormitori, le mense e i laboratori, molto piu' dettagliati di quelli per chi deve ancora candidarsi.
- Lezioni vere a cui si puo' assistere, e incontri diretti con i docenti e i presidi della facolta' a cui si e' stati ammessi.
- Fiera delle associazioni studentesche, dei club e delle squadre, con l'occasione di parlare con chi gia' studia li'.
- Sportelli amministrativi per borse di studio, financial aid e assegnazione degli alloggi.
- La Fraternity & Sorority Row apre i portici: e' la prima volta che le case si fanno vedere ai futuri pledge, mesi prima della rush vera di fine agosto.

Si va in famiglia, non da soli, e questo cambia il tono di tutto: i genitori fanno le domande sui soldi e sugli alloggi mentre i figli guardano altro.

E' il primo giorno in cui un futuro studente cammina sul campus come qualcuno che potrebbe restarci.
</admitted_student_days>

name: 2024-04-22 Compleanno dei gemelli e festa di Wulfnic
content:
<festa_dei_gemelli>
Da lunedi' 22 a giovedi' 25 aprile 2024, Bloodmoon Pack Territory.

Alyssa e Jasper compiono diciannove anni il 22 aprile. Wulfnic ha convocato i branchi di tutto il continente nordamericano per una festa di quattro giorni. Nessuno gliel'ha chiesto e nessuno gli dira' di no: e' l'Alpha of Alphas, quando chiama si va.

LA LUNA PIENA CADE MARTEDI' 23 APRILE, il secondo giorno. E' la notte in cui il branco e' al massimo, ed e' li' che la festa ha il suo centro.

IL PRECEDENTE. Wulfnic ha gia' fatto esattamente questo nel giugno 1994, per i diciannove anni di sua figlia Nixara. In quell'occasione Nixara ed Erik si scelsero a vicenda, ed e' da li' che discende tutto il resto.

IL PESO. Nixara e' morta il 22 aprile 2005 dando alla luce i gemelli. Il loro compleanno e' l'anniversario della morte della madre, e Wulfnic sta scegliendo di celebrarlo rifacendo la festa che quella storia l'ha messa in moto. Non e' un richiamo affettuoso: e' un uomo che riavvolge il nastro, davanti a un continente di testimoni, con la nipote che il culto considera Hvit tornata.
COSA E' DAVVERO. Non e' una festa di compleanno con un contorno politico. E' la presentazione di Alyssa secondo la legge del diciannovesimo anno: il raduno che la Casa convoca perche' un'Omega di sangue nobile incontri i propri pretendenti. La scelta resta sua e nessuno puo' esserle assegnato, ma la stanza la organizza suo nonno, e suo nonno e' l'Alpha of Alphas.

Gli obblighi sono due e sono minimi: un appuntamento, e un fidanzamento non vincolante. Il che vuol dire che, salvo che il gioco non trovi il modo di romperlo, Alyssa esce da quei quattro giorni promessa a qualcuno. Non e' un matrimonio, non e' un legame, si puo' sciogliere quando vuole e senza spiegazioni. Ma e' stato promesso davanti a un continente, e romperlo sara' pubblico esattamente quanto lo e' stato farlo.

Ecco perche' viene tutto il continente, perche' dura quattro giorni, e perche' cade sulla luna piena. Ed e' esattamente quello che accadde a Nixara nel giugno 1994.

QUANTO MANCA. Il World apre il 5 aprile 2024. Sono diciassette giorni. La domanda che Erik fa ai gemelli in cucina quella sera, su cosa vogliano fare della propria vita, arriva meno di tre settimane prima del raduno in cui sua figlia dovrebbe scegliersi un compagno.
</festa_dei_gemelli>

name: 2024-05-01 National College Decision Day
content:

Mercoledi' 1 maggio 2024.

Negli Stati Uniti il primo maggio e' il National College Decision Day: la data entro cui chi e' stato ammesso deve confermare l'immatricolazione e accettare il posto. Le domande si presentano mesi prima, in autunno; le lettere di ammissione arrivano in primavera; e questo e' il termine ultimo per rispondere. Chi non conferma entro oggi perde il posto, e per entrare l'anno dopo rifa' l'intera trafila.

Vale in tutto lo stato, SUCC e CUMS comprese, ed e' la ragione per cui gli Admitted Student Days si tengono ad aprile: sono l'ultima occasione che un ateneo ha di convincere qualcuno prima di questa data.

Per Alyssa e Jasper e' la fine dell'anno sabbatico preso dopo il diploma del giugno 2023. Qualunque cosa decidano, la decidono entro oggi.
</decision_day>

name: 2024-08-26 Primo giorno alla SUCC
content:
<primo_giorno_succ>
Lunedi' 26 agosto 2024. Inizio del primo semestre alla Supernatural University of Central California.

Campus di Solarton, a quaranta minuti di macchina da Seven Hills. Assemblea inaugurale ad Archer Wolfwood Hall, banchetti delle societa' studentesche sul Lunar Quad, sistemazione nei dormitori.

E' anche la settimana della rush greca: le dieci case della Fraternity & Sorority Row aprono ai pledge. Scarlett Rose vuole proporre Alyssa alla Theta Iota Theta. Noah vuole portare Jasper alla Kappa Sigma Alpha, come ogni maschio Douglas prima di lui.

Nessuno dei due esiti e' deciso: si gioca.
LA CERIMONIA DEGLI ALLOGGI. Ad Archer Wolfwood Hall i primi cinquanta della graduatoria d'ingresso vengono chiamati sul palco uno alla volta, in ordine di rango. Il merito non da' un titolo e non da' una casa: da' la priorita' nella scelta della propria stanza, e chi arriva prima sceglie meglio. Chi resta fuori dai primi cinquanta prende quello che avanza.

La chiamata e' anche il momento in cui si formalizza pubblicamente l'interesse per la rush greca. Non e' un'assegnazione e non vincola nessuno: e' una dichiarazione, davanti a tutto il campus, di quali case si intende provare. Il che significa che chiunque abbia interesse su una matricola sa esattamente quando quella matricola sara' in piedi su un palco, e cosa dira'.

Per i gemelli vuol dire che la domanda che hanno schivato da aprile arriva con un microfono davanti.
</primo_giorno_succ>

Cade anche il giorno del compleanno di Erik Douglas, nato il 31 ottobre 1969.

Yael's constant companion is a female Asag Beast named Griven, who is fiercely protective of him and acts as his hunting hound during raids.

The environment is harsh, cold, and claustrophobic. Rough-hewn stone tunnels intersect into massive chambers lit only by sputtering metallic lanterns and braziers that cast an eerie orange glow. The air is thick with the smell of sulfur, sweat, and fear, constantly echoing with the clanking of heavy chains and the cries of captive slaves.
